ALPHABET CENTER · LETTER D

Letter D — Dog.

A happy orange dog with its tail up, for the letter D. If your family has a dog, this card will be requested every single day.

Meet the letter, hear its sound, trace it together — then play. Everything on this page is free, gentle and paced for you.

THE LETTER SOUND

What does D say?

“d — duh, like dog”

D says duh, a quick tongue tap behind the teeth, like the start of dog. Say it fast — duh — and never duh-uh; the short version is the one that helps with reading.

TRACE THE LETTER

Trace D d together.

Follow the numbers with a finger — on screen or on each other’s palms. The arrows show the way to go, the numbers show where to start, and a grown-up reads the little script below each card. Slow and wobbly is exactly right.

Trace the uppercase D

Start at 1 at the top left, pull straight down. Lift. Start at 2 at the top of the stem, curve out to the right and round the big bowl back to the bottom of the stem.

Trace the lowercase d

Start at 1 at the top right of the bowl, sweep round to the left and all the way round. Lift. Start at 2 at the top, pull straight down past the bottom line.

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

Dog tricks.

Two minutes is plenty. Follow your child’s lead and stop while it is still fun — that is the whole method.

  1. 01

    Pretend to be dogs together: pant d, d, d.

  2. 02

    Teach your dog a trick — roll over, sit, stay — saying duh with each command.

  3. 03

    Finish with a big dog shake and a laugh.

PLAY & PRACTICE

Games that use this letter.

The games mix every letter — play them after meeting two or three letters, or any day your child asks. No scores, no timers, no wrong answers that count.
